source-integrity.freshness: current through 2026-09-24 market close; operating primary evidence through Q2 2026
source-integrity.sourceIndependence: primary issuer/SEC operating evidence plus independent current market evidence
source-integrity.rawVsDerivedConsistency: Q2 issuer release and SEC 10-Q are consistent on reported operating results; valuation evidence is separately identified as market-derived
source-integrity.evidenceAging: Q2 operating evidence remains current pending Q3; market price refreshed 2026-09-24

claims: Q2 2026 revenue was $60.801B, up 28% YoY, while operating margin fell to 31% from 43% as costs and infrastructure spending accelerated.
Advertising scale remains strong, but 2026 AI infrastructure intensity creates a material return-on-capital conversion test.
META closed at $777.59 on 2026-09-24 after a sharp September rally, reducing valuation headroom versus earlier evidence.

thesisQuality.basis: 28% revenue growth with simultaneous double-digit ad-impression and ad-price growth demonstrates exceptional current product-market fit and value capture; durability is capped below exceptional by AI-capex conversion uncertainty.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Revenue growth is strong and liquidity is substantial, but operating margin compressed to 31% and Q2 free cash flow was only $784M amid $31.08B capex.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: At the 2026-09-24 close of $777.59 and near-$2T market capitalization after a sharp rally, valuation requires continued strong growth and AI conversion; current independent evidence describes forward earnings multiples in the low-to-high 20s rather than clear deep-value asymmetry.

catalystScore.basis: Recent consumer AI product momentum and commercial integrations provide identifiable near-term monetization tests, while Q3 earnings provide a scheduled operating read-through; evidence is strong but some catalyst economics remain early.

governancePower.basis: SEC reporting and operating execution are established, but current run lacks a fresh proxy-level independent governance package sufficient to justify a strong-band score; uncertainty is treated conservatively.

alignment2036.basis: Scaled digital communications, AI systems and advertising infrastructure are durable technology capabilities with broad economic relevance, though not all investment necessarily maps to critical human infrastructure.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Family-of-apps monetization, AI recommendation systems, messaging and emerging AI products reuse compute/model infrastructure across multiple products, but advertising remains the dominant economic engine.

bottleneckControl.basis: Meta controls massive user distribution, data, model deployment and compute investment, creating meaningful capability constraints for competitors, but underlying compute/power supply is externally dependent and not uniquely controlled.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Large cash generation and diversified global app usage support resilience, while high fixed AI infrastructure commitments increase downside sensitivity if monetization lags.

substitutionResilience.basis: Scale, network effects and advertiser tooling create replacement friction, but user attention and AI interfaces remain intensely competitive and technologically substitutable.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Financial capacity supports procurement, but the current AI build depends on large external semiconductor, power and data-center supply chains; current evidence does not demonstrate exceptional redundancy.

pricingPower.basis: Average price per ad rose 12% while ad impressions rose 14%, directly demonstrating strong current monetization and pricing capture at scale.

riskEvidence.basis: Primary risks are unusually high AI infrastructure capital intensity, margin compression, legal/regulatory exposure and uncertain incremental return on newest capex; strong core demand and liquidity prevent a high-risk classification.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Identity/tradability are validated; operating claims are supported by issuer and SEC primary evidence and current valuation by independent market evidence. Confidence is reduced because governance evidence is not refreshed to a proxy-level package and AI-capex project returns remain undisclosed.

scoreRecord.thesis: Meta combines exceptional advertising monetization scale with AI-driven product optionality, but the investment case now depends materially on converting a very large infrastructure cycle into durable incremental engagement, advertiser performance and new revenue streams.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: AI/data-center capex grows faster than durable monetization and compresses free-cash-flow conversion and returns on capital.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Q3 2026 operating results and evidence that recent AI-product adoption converts into measurable monetization or efficiency gains.

risks: AI infrastructure capital intensity and return-on-capital uncertainty
margin compression if cost growth outruns monetization
unknowns: Project-level return on newest AI capex is undisclosed.
Fresh proxy-level governance detail was not acquired in this run.
